observation: All 528 arms were admitted and replayed, and every unsafe control distinguished. Two protected direct-Activity arms in the same silent-progress fanout-128 stratum failed only the frozen safety bound: detection took 5.270 and 8.902 seconds against a 5-second limit. Their replacement recoveries took 16 and 211 milliseconds, with zero false-positive revocations and zero accepted stale actions. The third direct repetition detected in 3.614 seconds; all three child-Workflow mates detected in 3.3-3.4 seconds.
inference: The protected procedure waits three deterministic Workflow seconds after accepted progress, then schedules the authority-revocation/replacement Activity on the same work task queue as the entire 128-item cohort. Under direct-Activity scheduling, the control Activity can sit behind the bulk workload long enough to miss the bound. Child scheduling happened to interleave the task earlier. This is an application control-plane capacity defect exposed by the topology comparison, not a Temporal guarantee or an evidence-harness error.
falsifier: A trace showing that the protected replacement Activity was dispatched promptly on an uncongested queue while detection still exceeded five seconds, or a repeated direct/fanout-128 run that misses the bound after the replacement is isolated on a verified control queue, would falsify this diagnosis.
correction: Route only the protected silent-progress replacement Activity through the existing effect/control task queue and register that Activity there for both topology arms. Keep initial work, the frozen three-second Workflow timer, the five-second oracle bound, and all unsafe behavior unchanged. Add deterministic routing coverage plus three real direct/fanout-128 repetitions, then execute a new append-only pilot root. Preserve v4 as rejected.
